PullRequest.Title: Sign macOS server binaries
PullRequest.Body:
Sign macOS server binaries during build.
Fixes #287005

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, serial await, two callers, package contents, and pre-package critical-path placement are directly visible. Exact wall-clock cost and native-binary count vary by product mix and timestamp-service latency, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: A separate codesign subprocess and secure-timestamp operation for every Mach-O file in both server distributions
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Critical-path time grows linearly with the number of Mach-O executables and native modules across the regular and web server trees; effective concurrency is one because every spawn is awaited before the next file and the two script invocations are also sequential.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased macOS production-build latency and reduced release-pipeline throughput, with exposure to accumulated timestamp-service latency or timeouts.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The server and web-server trees were packaged immediately after building, with no per-binary codesign subprocess or timestamp request on this path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new recursive loop scans each complete server tree and awaits `codesign --timestamp` once for every Mach-O file; the pipeline invokes the script for the regular server and then the web server before either archive can be packaged.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 63 awaits `spawn('codesign', ...)` inside the added per-file loop; together with added `--timestamp` at line 67 and the two new sequential callers, this changes the prior zero-call path into one boundary call per discovered Mach-O in each server tree.
Findings.Title: Bound the per-binary codesign fan-out
Findings.Impact: A production build for each macOS architecture now serializes signing of the Node executable and retained native dependencies/extensions in both server variants. As that native-binary set grows, each subprocess startup and timestamp round trip is added to the packaging critical path instead of overlapping, potentially adding substantial release latency.
Findings.Evidence: `packageTask` in build/gulpfile.reh.ts includes the Node runtime, production dependencies, built-in extensions, and extension dependencies in both server variants; build/.moduleignore explicitly retains many native `.node` files and helper executables. Changed line 63 places an awaited process spawn inside the recursive Mach-O loop, and line 67 requests a timestamp. The changed pipeline runs this script twice sequentially at product-build-darwin-compile.yml:222-223 before packaging at lines 247-260.
Findings.Recommendation: Collect the Mach-O paths and sign them with a small bounded worker pool (including an explicit concurrency cap compatible with keychain and timestamp-service limits), or omit secure timestamps from this temporary local signature if the subsequent ESRP signing replaces it. Preserve completion before packaging and propagate any worker failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Production macOS server and web-server build, local signing, and packaging for each architecture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Both server trees are built, then the client is signed, then the new server-signing step must finish before either server ZIP is created and before detached ESRP processing can begin. This work is therefore on the artifact-production critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively enumerate each server distribution and open/read/close the first four bytes of every file to identify Mach-O binaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two full recursive scans per production architecture, one for the regular server and one for the web server; file operations scale with every packaged file, with no grouping or cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Server directories were zipped after build without this additional scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both scans run synchronously before packaging can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run `codesign --timestamp` for each discovered Mach-O file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess and secure-timestamp operation per Mach-O across both trees. The package graph contains Node plus production native dependencies and extension binaries; duplicate binaries in the two independently packaged variants are signed separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local per-binary server codesign or timestamp operations occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each call is awaited serially, and the two tree-level script invocations are sequential, so durations sum before packaging.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compress the regular and web server trees into ZIP archives.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two archive operations per production architecture, unchanged from the prior build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two ZIP operations ran immediately after each server build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still blocks ESRP submission, but is moved later so signed content is archived.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total packaged-file count controls scan I/O; total Mach-O executable/native-module count across both distributions controls codesign subprocess and timestamp cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filesystem probing and codesign are serial within each tree; the regular and web tree scripts also run serially, yielding effective codesign concurrency of one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache, deduplication, or reuse between the regular and web server scans/signatures; every production build repeats all work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the recursive traversal, per-match awaited subprocess, timestamp option, duplicated callers, and pipeline ordering are directly established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact file/native-binary counts and timestamp latency vary by product quality, extensions, architecture, and Apple service conditions, but the linear serialized boundary fan-out is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out because the diff introduces unbounded-by-design serial subprocess/network work proportional to native-binary count on the production packaging critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Detached ESRP signing and notarization of macOS client, DMG, server, and web-server archives
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The ESRP process starts after all local packaging. It is detached and can overlap configured test jobs, but the post-job attach must complete before signed artifacts are moved and published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke ESRP MacAppDeveloperSign for each artifact archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four concurrent jobs per architecture after the change: the prior client and DMG jobs plus one regular-server and one web-server job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only client and DMG signing jobs ran, two concurrently; server archives were published unsigned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the test critical path while detached, but required before final artifact publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke ESRP MacAppNotarize for each signed artifact archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four concurrent jobs per architecture after signing completes, versus two previously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only client and DMG notarization jobs ran.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can overlap no further tests once reached inside the detached worker and must finish before post-job attachment/publication.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed artifact count per architecture: client, DMG, regular server, and web server.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All four signing processes start together; after all are observed complete, all four notarization processes start together. Concurrency is a fixed four, not proportional to package contents.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No local cache or coalescing is present; each distinct artifact requires its own signing and notarization operation. Warm-cache behavior is not applicable to these unique build outputs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the four-way concurrency and detached ordering; insufficient evidence that the bounded increase breaches ESRP limits or slows the maximum-duration batch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote service duration and contention are unknown, but cardinality is fixed and the two added operations correspond to two newly signed artifacts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the added remote work is required for the two new signed artifacts, remains bounded, and runs concurrently rather than creating collection-scaled fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI-only macOS server compilation without production signing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When VSCODE_CIBUILD is true, the production-only signing, packaging, ESRP, and publication block is skipped; compilation remains the relevant critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create server and web-server ZIP archives.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two compression passes were removed from the CI-only path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each server build immediately created one ZIP even for CI builds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes these operations from CI builds rather than adding cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Server and web-server artifact byte size/file count formerly controlled compression time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two old ZIP operations were sequential build steps; neither now runs in CI-only builds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache was involved before or after.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from YAML conditional scope and moved packaging steps.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The CI configurations that depend on these archives are not material to a performance regression; performance work is strictly reduced on this branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: this path performs less compression work after the diff.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files. Traced release and CI pipeline ordering, recursive filesystem work, per-binary local signing/timestamp subprocesses, ZIP creation, detached ESRP signing/notarization, cache behavior, and effective concurrency. Submitted one medium-confidence/high-mechanism-confidence boundary-fanout finding for serialized per-Mach-O codesign work; the fixed four-artifact ESRP concurrency and CI packaging removal do not warrant findings.
